hypothesis: The nonzero ONNX output destabilizes standing through a specific anatomical action family rather than through inference, target dispatch, controls, or the passive plant. Post-inference family masking will identify the smallest action family sufficient to reproduce collapse.

locked_configuration.action_axis: observation-parent-bind mesh-component axis from first policy

action_groups.lower: Proto joints 0-7: hips, knees, ankles, toes
action_groups.axial: Proto joints 8-12: torso, spine, chest, neck, head
action_groups.arms: Proto joints 13-22: thorax, shoulders, elbows, wrists, hands

arms.name: lower_only
arms.conditioned_actions: lower group retained; axial and arms zero

arms.name: axial_only
arms.conditioned_actions: axial group retained; lower and arms zero

arms.name: arms_only
arms.conditioned_actions: arms group retained; lower and axial zero

single_changed_variable: Which post-conditioning anatomical action family is retained. Raw ONNX output, observations, inference, cadence, and every downstream stage remain unchanged.
validity_gates: All arms use the same clean behavior commit and reused binary.
First-policy input and raw model output are byte-identical across all arms.
Masked conditioned outputs contain exactly the preregistered retained indices.
Inference cadence and target readback ratio remain valid in every arm.
The zero arm passes the locked ten-second hold; otherwise the ablation is invalid.
support: At least one single-family arm reproduces the all-actions failure while another single-family arm passes, localizing a sufficient causal family.
interaction_result: All single-family arms pass but all-actions fails, proving a cross-family interaction and requiring pairwise combinations next.
falsification: Every single-family arm fails similarly, so no anatomical family localization is supported.
next: Subdivide the sufficient family, or test pairwise combinations if the result is interactive, until the minimum failing joint subset is identified.
